### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**24** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **186** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a182fbe37765ab486f3aa5e372ffa9d6af1f6758` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a4fa7e0a1847997eccfb363c86e53f94606324f0` — the merge of head `e9bdc06989526a16dde9a6d8433b7d615ca7608e` into base `a182fbe37765ab486f3aa5e372ffa9d6af1f6758`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a4fa7e0a1847997eccfb363c86e53f94606324f0 && git checkout a4fa7e0a1847997eccfb363c86e53f94606324f0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a182fbe37765ab486f3aa5e372ffa9d6af1f6758 e9bdc06989526a16dde9a6d8433b7d615ca7608e && git checkout -B drift-repro a182fbe37765ab486f3aa5e372ffa9d6af1f6758 && git merge --no-ff e9bdc06989526a16dde9a6d8433b7d615ca7608e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a182fbe37765ab486f3aa5e372ffa9d6af1f6758
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Final green head for L1 and same-head contract review (2026-11-25T19:13Z): `40ea9d1225`.

- **Checks at this head:** 58 `success`, 11 skipped (all 11 expected per `check-expected-skips`, exit 0), 0 failed. `Test UI (9/16)` failed once on an unrelated `AuthProvider.test.tsx` case (flake judgement 7171103696) and passed on its one re-run (attempt 2). `mergeable_state: clean`.
- **Size:** 12 files, +341 / −33; not governed (0 of 12 paths hit the register); `Fixes #37273`.
- **Declaration:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: `@objectstack/core`'s exported `operationUserMessage` gains an optional third argument, `params`; existing calls are unchanged. `Metadata-protocol: none`. The claim amendment is 7170597182.
- **What it does:** the `/actions` door's forward-unavailable `503` and the own-door bridge's two `501`s now come from the operation-message catalog (`BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES`, `packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts`) in en / zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES, with the English byte-identical. Ablations restoring the hard-coded English turn the zh pins red (2 of 3, and 2 of 5), and the files were restored to the HEAD blob. spec, core, runtime and service-print suites are green. 94 of 96 derived gates ran; 2 were NOT MEASURED (shallow-clone history; full build).
- **For the contract review:** the PR edits the published catalog in `packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` (new keys and header text) and declares a widening on `@objectstack/core`.
- **Out of scope:** the personal-view and attachment own-door doors still answer their `501` in English (they name no noun key). Filed as a follow-up after this lands.
- **Overlap:** `overlap-check` VERDICT clean.

## 席位核对 — REWORK · L1 · head `40ea9d1225b80f03cf0aa6120e8851484573c453` · 2026-11-25T19:44Z

PR #37336 for card #37273. Read against GitHub and the head tree, not against the report. One open item, on the changeset prose only; the code, the pins and the declaration all hold.

**Open items**

- S1 (should-fix) — `.changeset/37273-print-path-locale.md`, third paragraph: "a request in English, with no `Accept-Language`, or in a language the catalog carries no text for, reads the same sentence as before." This is false for the `/actions` door's `503` in a workspace whose default locale is one the catalog carries. The door reads the execution context, and `assemble-execution-context.ts:425` folds `locale` to the workspace default when the request names none; `operationUserMessage` then tries `locale`, then `workspaceLocale`. Measured on the head's `operationUserMessage` with `action_forward_unavailable`: no header with a zh-CN workspace default answers Chinese; a `fr` header with a zh-CN workspace default answers Chinese; an `en-US` header with a zh-CN workspace default answers English; no header and no default answers English. The changeset's own second paragraph states the ladder, so the two paragraphs disagree, and the changeset is what ships as `CHANGELOG.md`. Fix: scope that sentence to the bridge's `501`, and say that at the `/actions` door a request with no `Accept-Language`, or with a language the catalog lacks, takes the workspace default before `en`. The behaviour is the card's and stays. The delta is one changeset sentence, so the head's contract record keeps governing under the prose-only exception.

**Shape**

- Open, draft, base `main`; the body's first content line is `Fixes #37273` and no closing keyword binds another card (`l1-face.mjs --pr 37336`). `Fixes` is right: both sites, one pin per site, the ablation and every carried nit are delivered.
- 12 files, +341 / −33. Not governed. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` read `declared` in the PR body and in the changeset body.
- `l1-face` flags one item, `changeset`: `@objectstack/service-print` is touched with no entry. Cleared by reading: the one file is `src/print-routes.test.ts`, and the package's `files[]` is `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, so nothing from that package publishes.

**Premise and fix, measured**

- The fix matches the card and direction 7159533198: only the wire `message` is localized, no `userMessage` is added, and code and status are unchanged. Every new pin asserts `status` and `code` and that `userMessage` is undefined.
- English is byte-identical. The merge-base's hard-coded `apiActionForwardUnavailableError` and the head's catalog rendering agree over 12 cases (3 action shapes × 4 door values). Both bridge sentences agree with the old template literals.
- Catalog completeness: 4 locales (en, zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES), 42 keys each, identical key sets; 0 placeholder mismatches over all 42 keys × 4 locales. The six new keys carry `{{action}}`, `{{target}}` (two keys), `{{door}}`, `{{slot}}`, `{{producer}}` (one), `{{door}}`, `{{slot}}`, `{{member}}` (one) and none (two) in every locale.
- Carried nits: the five rewordings equal comment 7160569088 character for character; the three header notes are present and true against `print-routes.ts:340`, `preferredLocaleFromHeader` and `server-fault-log.ts:284`; the N4 `/srv/secret` assertions sit on fixtures that do throw that path.
- Widening is pure: `operationUserMessage` gains an optional third parameter, nothing is removed, no required member is added, and a two-argument call builds the same render input as before. The only strings that change for existing callers are the five non-English `print_*` rewordings the card ordered.

**Pins and ablation, re-run by this review** (throwaway worktree at the head, removed afterwards; under the shared verify lock)

- Head: `own-door-bridge.test.ts`, `api-action-forward.test.ts`, `action-dispatch.test.ts` with `-t 37273`: 3 files passed, 8 tests passed. Core `operation-user-message.test.ts`: 9 passed. Spec `operation-message.test.ts`: 60 passed.
- Ablation A, `action-execution.ts` restored to the merge-base blob (`5a34a39a17df` to `e064365170c3`): 2 failed, 6 passed. The REST zh-CN pin and the host-door pin went red; the English controls stayed green.
- Ablation B, `own-door-bridge.ts` restored to the merge-base blob (`0b5835a501bb` to `074034f16dea`): 2 failed, 6 passed. Both zh-CN `501` pins went red; the controls and the no-noun-key pin stayed green.
- Ablation C, core `operation-user-message.ts` restored to the merge-base blob: 1 failed, 8 passed (the `params` pin).
- After each run the file's hash equalled the head blob and `git status` was empty.

**Gates**

- Check-runs at the head (69): 58 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 pending. All 11 skips are on the expected roster (`l1-face`: 0 unexpected skip). `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are `success`. `Test UI (9/16)` is `success` on its re-run; the flake judgement is PR comment 7171103696 and the PR touches nothing under `ui/**`.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main` at `a182fbe377`: clean, exit 0. `landing-k`: K = 9, below the hold at 15; no new locale pack, no shared book moved.

**Changeset**

- Levels are right: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/runtime` at `patch`. The kind is `none`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3).
- Sentence read: paragraphs one and two hold against the diff, including the six key names, the ladder and the `params` sentence. Paragraph three: its first sentence is S1; its second (the rewordings and the header notes) holds.

**Maintainer summary ("维护者速读")**

- Accurate on what changes, why, and the failure mode ("错误码与状态码都不变"). "要你做什么：无" is right for an ungoverned PR.
- See N4 for one narrow wording.

**Nits**

- N1 — the six new keys have no spec-level placeholder pin, unlike the catalog's other families ("every locale defines all N, each with exactly its own placeholders"). zh-CN is pinned through the runtime literals; a dropped placeholder in ja-JP or es-ES would pass. Parity is measured clean at this head.
- N2 — in ja-JP and es-ES the door and the unnamed-target noun are the same word (`エンドポイント`, `punto de acceso`), so an action with no string target reads "target (endpoint) this endpoint forwards". Wording only.
- N3 — `OwnDoorBridge.nounKey` is a free string. A key the catalog lacks would print the key as the noun, and nothing pins that a bridge's key renders its `noun` in English. The one bridge that sets it is correct.
- N4 — the maintainer summary says "打印类操作", but the `503` changes for every same-origin `type: 'api'` action whose forward is unavailable.
- N5 — the report's "no build leg: the runtime tests import src" does not hold on a fresh tree: the three runtime files fail to load until the dependency closure is built (`@objectstack/metadata` entry), and core's test reads spec's built `system` entry. The readings above were taken after `turbo run build` over runtime's dependencies.

**Accepted deviations**

- `Clause-②` measured `yes (widening)` against the claim's expected `no`: confirmed, see the contract record.
- `packages/services/service-print/src/print-routes.test.ts` and `packages/core/src/utils/operation-user-message.test.ts` are outside the claim's first file list; both are test-only and named in amendment 7170597182.
- The dev's first edits landed in the shared checkout before it moved to a worktree. The shared tree reads clean now.

**Seat-side items**

- The card's newest `Claim:` comment is 7169220062 (2026-11-25T17:14Z). `readClause2Line` reads it `declared` / `no` / no arm. Amendment 7170597182 (2026-11-25T18:12Z) is not a `Claim:` comment, and its bulleted, bold line reads `malformed`. The queue gate reads the claim comment's line-initial key only, so the seat owes a new `Claim:` comment with the line `Clause-②: yes (widening)` before enqueueing.
- Out of scope: the personal-view and attachment doors still answer their `501` in English. The PR body says `carrier: none`; PR comment 7172022330 (2026-11-25T19:13Z) says the seat files it after landing. No card exists yet.
- The card and PR comments are signed by `session_01QSeKYnagJvGbCtNg2PhvgW`; this review is signed by the seat session in the first line.

**Landing**

- After the S1 patch: the seat reads the delta (changeset only), re-reads the checks at the new head, and the zone lands. K = 9 now; merge `main` first if K reaches 15.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `40ea9d1225b80f03cf0aa6120e8851484573c453`
Local-runs: probe — the seat's review order asked for the card's pins at the head and under ablation, run once in a throwaway worktree that is now removed
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/core/src/utils/operation-user-message.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/print.ts

PR #37336, card #37273. Read: the card and all six comments, seat direction 7159533198, the PR body, the full net diff against the merge-base, and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds, and it reads `declared` / `yes` / `widening` in the PR body and in the changeset body. `packages/core/src/index.ts:236` re-exports `operation-user-message.js`, and `packages/runtime/src/index.ts:432` re-exports all of `@objectstack/core`, so `operationUserMessage` is on both entries. It gains an optional third parameter, `params`.
- The widening is pure. Nothing is removed or renamed, no required member is added, and a two-argument call builds the same render input as before (the `params` key is spread in only when given). Core's pre-existing cases and the new "without params" case pass at the head.
- The catalog is declared as a string-keyed record of string-keyed records, so six new keys move no type. No key is removed. No English string of an existing key changes. Five non-English `print_*` strings are reworded, as the card orders, and they equal comment 7160569088 character for character.
- Not on a published entry: `OwnDoorBridge.nounKey` and the third parameter of `apiActionForwardUnavailableError`. `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` names neither `own-door-bridge` nor `action-execution`, and the package's `exports` address only `.` and `./compiled-plugin-manifest-file`.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no authorable key, value or metadata type moves. The new keys add no working `errors.*` override, because neither producer holds an `i18n` service, and the header says so.
- Completeness: en, zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES each define the same 42 keys; placeholder sets match English for every key in every locale (0 mismatches). English is byte-identical to the merge-base sentences over 12 action and door combinations for the `503` and for both `501` templates.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/runtime`: `patch`. Correct: the kind is `none`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3). No BREAKING banner is owed.
- `@objectstack/service-print` carries no entry and owes none: its one changed file is a test, outside the package's `files[]`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev report (card comment 7170542144) has no open question and no security finding. Its two flags are answered: the declaration measured `yes (widening)` against the claim's expected `no`, confirmed in ①; the two test files outside the first file list are test-only and named in amendment 7170597182.
- Direction 7159533198 is kept: only the wire `message` moves, no `userMessage` is added to a fault, and `code` and `status` are unchanged. Each new pin asserts all three.
- Interpolation is single-pass (`interpolateValidationMessage`), and the bridge renders its noun before handing it in as a value, so a placeholder inside an action name, a target or a noun is printed as written. The header-derived locale only selects a catalog; an unknown tag falls to English.
- SQL push-down: no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join is added.
- The PR's author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay note is owed.
- Checks at the head: 58 `success`, 11 `skipped` (all on the expected roster), 0 failed, 0 pending.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts`, against the card, the direction, and its first consumers in this diff:

- The six keys are the right unit. Two `503` sentences split by remedy (the deployment's HTTP server, or the kernel handed to `dispatchAction`), one noun for an unnamed target, two `501` sentences split by what is missing, and one door noun. Placing them in this catalog is what the card orders, and the header states that the `action_forward_*` sentences are an operator's, localized because the console shows a refused action's wire `message`.
- The header's new text is true against the code it cites. The print door has no `i18n` service and passes only a locale (`print-routes.ts:340`), so `errors.print_*` is not consulted and a top tag the catalog lacks answers English. `preferredLocaleFromHeader` takes the top tag with no q-value reading. `serverFaultLogMessage` (`server-fault-log.ts:284`) logs the thrown error's own message and falls back to the wire text only when that message is empty. The `/actions` door's ladder is `locale`, then `workspaceLocale`, then `en`, which is what `operationUserMessage` reads.
- Implementing files agree with the contract. `action-execution.ts` renders the `_host` key at the host door and the plain key elsewhere, quoting a string target and using the catalog noun otherwise. `action-dispatch.ts` passes the call's execution context. `own-door-bridge.ts` localizes only when the bridge names a noun key and otherwise keeps the whole sentence English; `print.ts` names `own_door_print`, whose English equals its `noun`.
- Pins, run by this review: at the head, 8 of 8 card pins pass in the three runtime files, 9 of 9 in core's file and 60 of 60 in the catalog's file. With `action-execution.ts` at the merge-base blob, 2 fail and 6 pass; with `own-door-bridge.ts` at the merge-base blob, 2 fail and 6 pass; with core's helper at the merge-base blob, 1 fails and 8 pass. Each file was restored to the head blob.

Findings: three nits, none affecting correctness or the contract.

- nit — the new keys have no spec-level placeholder pin of the kind the catalog's other families carry; ja-JP and es-ES placeholders are unpinned. Parity is clean at this head.
- nit — ja-JP and es-ES use one word for the door and for the unnamed-target noun, so that rare sentence reads circular.
- nit — `nounKey` is a free string; a key the catalog lacks would print the key as the noun.

The changeset prose is outside the contract faces and is read at L1.

Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYpEsWWE9Y5YtSsDgqZ`

**VERDICT: PASS**
